sources.relevant_excerpt: Designation of Qatar for the Visa Waiver Program (89 FR 78783, DHS final rule, 8 CFR 217.2): 'Designated country refers to Andorra, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brunei, Chile, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Monaco, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Qatar, Republic of Korea, San Marino, Singapore, Slovak Republic, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, and the United Kingdom. The United Kingdom refers only to British citizens who have the unrestricted right of permanent abode in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland, the Channel Islands, and the Isle of Man) ... Taiwan refers only to individuals who have unrestricted right of permanent abode on Taiwan and are in possession of an electronic passport bearing a personal identification (household registration) number.' ... 'Eligible citizens and nationals of VWP countries may apply for admission to the United States at U.S. ports of entry as nonimmigrant visitors for a period of ninety days or less for business or pleasure without first obtaining a nonimmigrant visa' ... conditions include: 'present a machine-readable, electronic passport'; 'possess a round-trip ticket, unless exempted'; 'obtain an approved travel authorization via the Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA)'; 'has not been present, at any time on or after March 1, 2011, in Iraq, Syria, a country that is designated by the Secretary of State as a state-sponsor of terrorism, or a country or area of concern'.
sources.effective_date_evidence: This final rule is effective on September 26, 2024. The Secretary's designation is effective on September 24, 2024. The designation will be implemented on December 1, 2024.

sources.search_query: federalregister.gov API: "electronic system for travel authorization" fee
sources.relevant_excerpt: Certain DHS Immigration Fees Required by HR-1: Fiscal Year 2026 Adjustments for Inflation (90 FR 52085): 'ESTA is the online system through which aliens intending to enter the United States under the Visa Waiver Program (VWP) must obtain an electronic travel authorization in advance of travel to the United States. Each alien intending to travel by air, sea, or land to the United States under the VWP must receive a travel authorization via ESTA prior to travel.' ... 'the inflation-adjusted FY 2026 ESTA fee will be $40.27 ($17 + $10.27 + $13) per travel authorization. In the event the ESTA application is denied, the FY 2026 fee is $10.27' ... 'EVUS is an online system currently used by nationals of the People's Republic of China (PRC) holding a 10-year B-1, B-2, or B-1/B-2 (visitor) visa to provide required information to DHS prior to travel to the United States. ... PRC nationals with an approved U.S.-issued visa of a designated category must enroll in EVUS and provide or update personal and travel information to receive a determination of travel eligibility.' ... 'the inflation-adjusted HR-1 EVUS fee for FY 2026 is $30.75 ($30 + $0.75)' ... 'the total fee to apply for a CBP Form I-94 at a land border port of entry for FY 2026 will continue to be $30, consisting of the $6 land border fee and the $24 HR-1 fee. CBP will not assess a fee for aliens arriving at an air or sea port of entry.'
sources.effective_date_evidence: CBP will begin assessing the FY 2026 amounts for the HR-1 I-94, ESTA, and EVUS fees described in this notice on January 1, 2026. [Initial HR-1 fee rates were assessed beginning September 30, 2025 per 90 FR 42025.]

sources.relevant_excerpt: CBP notice, Arrival and Departure Record (Form I-94) and Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA) (90 FR 57208): 'Romania Removal from Visa Waiver Program (VWP): Due to the removal of Romania from the approved list of countries under the VWP, CBP is updating relevant collections to reflect this removal. The public can refer to https://www.dhs.gov/visa-waiver-program for the list of approved countries under the VWP.' ... 'As an ESTA is required for any travel to the United States under the VWP, the collection is being updated to include travelers from current VWP designated countries' ... Guam-CNMI Visa Waiver (Form I-736): 'Public Law 110-229 provides for certain aliens to be exempt from the nonimmigrant visa requirement if seeking entry into Guam or the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI) as a visitor for a maximum stay of 45 days ... At the Secretary's discretion, passport holders of the People's Republic of China who are not in possession of a visitors' visa may be allowed to enter CNMI for up to 14 days under the discretionary parole authority.'

Machine-readable electronic passport (e-Passport) required
Round-trip ticket required unless exempted by statute or regulation

Ineligible if present in Iraq, Syria, a state sponsor of terrorism, or a designated country/area of concern on or after 2011-03-01 (statutory exemptions/waivers possible); such travelers must obtain a visa instead
GBR: applies only to British citizens with the unrestricted right of permanent abode in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland, the Channel Islands, and the Isle of Man)
TWN: applies only to individuals with unrestricted right of permanent abode on Taiwan holding an electronic passport bearing a personal identification (household registration) number
Romania was removed from the VWP (per CBP notice of 2025-12-10) and is not included
Travelers who prefer, or are ineligible for ESTA, may apply for a B-2 visitor visa instead
Consular B-2 tourist visa not needed for tourism stays of 90 days or less under the Visa Waiver Program with approved ESTA
A B-2 visitor visa is required for stays over 90 days or if the traveler is ineligible for the VWP/ESTA
8 CFR 212.1: a visa is generally not required for Canadian citizens and citizens of the British Overseas Territory of Bermuda (exceptions: E, K, S, V visa categories)
A valid passport is required (Canadian citizens may instead use NEXUS/FAST/SENTRI/INAC documents in specific circumstances)
Period of admission determined by CBP at the port of entry (maximum stay not verified from a fetched official source)
U.S. citizens and nationals are not subject to U.S. nonimmigrant visa or VWP/ESTA requirements; the VWP applies only to 'any person who is not a citizen or national of the United States'
Not a Visa Waiver Program designated nationality; B-2 visitor visa required for tourism
Apply via Form DS-160 and interview at a U.S. embassy or consulate; application processing fee USD 185
PRC nationals holding a 10-year B-1, B-2, or B-1/B-2 visa must additionally enroll in EVUS before travel (FY2026 enrollment fee USD 30.75)
Period of admission determined by CBP at the port of entry

Not Visa Waiver Program designated nationalities (Hong Kong SAR passport holders are not covered by the United Kingdom's VWP designation, which applies only to British citizens with right of abode in the UK)
B-2 visitor visa required for tourism: Form DS-160, interview at a U.S. embassy or consulate, application processing fee USD 185
Period of admission determined by CBP at the port of entry
Nationalities not designated for the Visa Waiver Program and not covered by a specific exemption (e.g., Canada/Bermuda) need a B-2 visitor visa for tourism
Form DS-160, interview at a U.S. embassy or consulate, application processing fee USD 185
Mexican nationals holding a valid biometric B-1/B-2 Border Crossing Card (Form DSP-150) do not need a separate visa or passport when entering from Mexico at a land port of entry (8 CFR 212.1)

policies.description: Citizens/nationals of designated countries may be admitted at U.S. ports of entry as nonimmigrant visitors for business or pleasure for 90 days or less without a visa, subject to eligibility conditions (e-passport, approved ESTA, round-trip ticket, travel-history restrictions for Iraq/Syria/state sponsors of terrorism since 2011-03-01, etc.). List per 8 CFR 217.2 as amended by the Qatar designation (89 FR 78783); Romania was subsequently removed from the approved list (CBP notice, 90 FR 57208, Dec 10, 2025). DHS maintains the current list at https://www.dhs.gov/visa-waiver-program (page not directly fetchable).
conditions: Machine-readable electronic passport (e-Passport)
Approved ESTA before travel (air, sea, and land)
Stay of 90 days or less for business or pleasure
Round-trip ticket unless exempted
No presence in Iraq, Syria, state sponsors of terrorism, or designated countries/areas of concern on/after 2011-03-01 (exemptions/waivers possible)
Waiver of right to review or appeal admissibility decisions (other than asylum)
UK designation limited to British citizens with right of permanent abode; Taiwan limited to e-passports with household registration number

policies.description: Mandatory online travel authorization for all Visa Waiver Program travelers arriving by air, sea, or land. Approval is generally valid for two years (or until passport expiry) and allows multiple visits. FY2026 fee USD 40.27 (USD 10.27 retained if the application is denied), assessed from January 1, 2026 under HR-1 (Public Law 119-21). Applications processed up to 72 hours. CBP has proposed making the ESTA Mobile application the sole application platform.
conditions: Required for every VWP traveler prior to travel
e-Passport required
ESTA validity: generally 2 years, multiple entries
Official application portal: https://esta.cbp.dhs.gov/

policies.description: Default channel for all nationalities not covered by the VWP or a specific exemption: apply to the Department of State with Form DS-160, attend an interview at a U.S. embassy or consulate, pay the USD 185 non-petition-based nonimmigrant visa application processing fee. Renewals must also be done at a U.S. embassy or consulate. Period of admission is determined by CBP at entry (B-2 admission period not verified from a fetched official source).
conditions: Form DS-160 application
Interview at a U.S. embassy or consulate
USD 185 application processing fee (22 CFR 22.1, Item 21)
Additional visa issuance (reciprocity) fee may apply for some nationalities (not verified)

policies.policy_name: Canada and Bermuda visa exemption / Western Hemisphere Travel Initiative (WHTI)
policies.description: Under 8 CFR 212.1, a visa is generally not required for Canadian citizens or citizens of the British Overseas Territory of Bermuda (exceptions: E, K, S, V categories). Passport required, with alternative WHTI-compliant documents (NEXUS, FAST, SENTRI, INAC card; birth certificate options for Canadian children at land/sea ports). Mexican nationals with a biometric B-1/B-2 Border Crossing Card (DSP-150) may enter from Mexico at land ports without a separate visa/passport.
conditions: Exceptions for E, K, S, V nonimmigrant categories (visa required)
Passport or approved WHTI-compliant document required
BCC facility applies to Mexican nationals at land ports of entry from Mexico

policies.description: Nationals of the People's Republic of China holding 10-year B-1, B-2, or B-1/B-2 visitor visas must enroll in EVUS and keep their information current to receive a determination of travel eligibility before traveling to the United States (8 CFR part 215, subpart B). FY2026 enrollment fee USD 30.75, assessed from January 1, 2026.
conditions: Applies to PRC-passport holders with 10-year B-1/B-2 category visas
Enrollment fee paid at time of enrollment

policies.description: Public Law 110-229 exempts certain nationalities from the nonimmigrant visa requirement for visits of up to 45 days limited to Guam or the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI). At the Secretary's discretion, PRC passport holders without a visitor visa may be allowed to enter the CNMI only for up to 14 days under discretionary parole. The list of eligible countries for this territorial program was not verified from a fetched official source.
conditions: Valid only for entry to Guam or CNMI, not the U.S. mainland
Form I-736 required (transition to mandatory electronic submission proposed)
PRC parole facility: CNMI only, up to 14 days
policies.maximum_stay: 45 days (Guam/CNMI); 14 days for PRC nationals paroled into CNMI

passport_validity.condition_text: Per USAGov (VWP context), passports must generally be valid for six months after the date the traveler plans to exit the U.S., though some countries have different requirements under country-specific agreements (the 'Six-Month Club' exemption list maintained by CBP could not be fetched). For visa applicants, 22 CFR 41.104 requires a passport valid for the period required by INA 212(a)(7)(B)(i)(I) (six months beyond the intended period of stay, subject to bilateral agreement exceptions).
